searchText: Hello everyone a question regarding locked eth ... After Ethereum moves to POS will the locked ethereum be accessible or we have to wait until shard chains ? <@!315530255446179840> Withdrawals likely go into some fork in-between those events. Withdrawals are a complex mechanism that needs additional testing, review, etc. and thus not part of the Merge upgrade if we take the fastest route to proof of stake. Withdrawals require simultaneous upgrade of consensus and execution layers which increases the complexity WAG, do we have an estimate on the withdrawal timeframe post-merge? 1 month? 1 quarter? 1 half? etc.. I do believe it will help folks to grasp the window when they could exit being a valdiator (and get their ETH back) and counterintuitively, the moment that we allow for withdraws, I am convinced the deposit contract will spike with new deposits.. Definitely not 1 month. I'd say ~6 is realistic? It's basically another hard fork, and we may want to do more than just enabling withdrawals (e.g. if there are a bunch of EIPs that have been pending for 1 year by then, it can makes sense to bundle the upgrade) thank you. for some context and specific for the withdrawal capability, would this be a beaconchain hf or execution hf or both ? thx I think they answered that above explaining that the withdrawals complexity stems from needing a HF for BOTH layers simultaneously Curiously. If the withdrawals process is as shown in the latest demo why isn’t it possible to HF the execution layer separately since sending proofs to the withdrawal context will yield nothing. And then HF the consensus layer? Contract *
